scenarios.name: wildcard-cert-private-staging
scenarios.rationale: Both use DNS-01 with --dns-cloudflare, a credentials file at mode 600, and both -d names, and both explain that the wildcard doesn't cover the bare domain; A spells out the token scope (Zone→DNS→Edit on the specific zone) in dashboard steps, while B states the scope more briefly but correctly, so A is slightly more complete on the token-scoping point.

scenarios.name: nginx-https-with-reload-hook
scenarios.rationale: Both install Certbot, issue the cert with `certbot --nginx -d shop.northwind.dev`, verify with `certbot renew --dry-run`, add a deploy hook in `/etc/letsencrypt/renewal-hooks/deploy/`, and avoid force-renewal on production; A mentions `fullchain.pem` explicitly and notes the nginx plugin reloads, while B gives more verification steps and correctly says dry-run does not run deploy hooks but never names the cert paths.

scenarios.name: traefik-docker-compose-https
scenarios.rationale: Both meet every core rubric item (Traefik v3, HTTP challenge on web, persistent ACME volume, ports 80/443, Host/websecure/certresolver labels, HTTP→HTTPS redirect, staging caserver and Docker-socket caveat); B adds an explicit server port label, .env email and a private-registry note, while A gives a clearer socket caveat and a more cautious optional port label, so they are nearly equal.
